items.headline: Trump lands in China for summit with Xi and Putin
items.summary: President Trump arrived in southern China after signing a trade deal with the Philippines, ahead of meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the Asia-Pacific summit. Russia used the gathering to describe Europe as in "humiliating decline."

items.headline: Iran targets U.S. base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain
items.summary: Iran widened its Gulf attacks, striking at a U.S. air base in Kuwait and at sites in Bahrain. Tehran said the attacks answered U.S. drone surveillance and an attack on Iranian communications towers.

items.headline: Peltola wins Alaska, Democrats' ninth Senate flip
items.summary: Former Rep. Mary Peltola defeated Sen. Dan Sullivan, the last Senate race to be decided. Democrats flipped nine Republican seats, their biggest midterm Senate gain in nearly 70 years.

items.headline: House Democrats nominate Jeffries for speaker
items.summary: House Democrats broadly backed Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, putting him in line to become the first Black speaker of the House. A small number of Democrats voted against his nomination.

items.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share
items.summary: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. The price came in higher than expected despite worries about an AI bubble and Nvidia's leadership turmoil.

items.headline: Storm floods South Florida
items.summary: A slow-moving storm fueled by El Niño dumped heavy rain on South Florida, prompting an emergency declaration. Roads flooded, vehicles were submerged and a synagogue roof collapsed.

items.headline: U.S. fossil fuel emissions set to fall this year
items.summary: U.S. fossil fuel emissions are expected to drop this year as coal power and gasoline demand decline. The decrease comes despite surging electricity demand and federal support for coal.

items.headline: Incoming Oversight chair puts Trump allies on notice
items.summary: Rep. Robert Garcia, set to chair the House Oversight Committee, sent document-preservation letters to Trump family members and administration allies. The letters signal investigations Democrats plan once they take the House majority.

items.headline: U.S. foreign aid restarts with uneven terms
items.summary: The Trump administration is restarting foreign aid after dismantling USAID, using new agreements with recipient countries. Zambia and Zimbabwe face different approaches and shared uncertainty over what comes next.

items.headline: NSA's classified network disrupted
items.summary: The National Security Agency's classified network suffered a disruption this week. TIME examines what the outage could mean for national security.

digest.overview:
Democrats completed their midterm Senate sweep as Mary Peltola unseated Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, a ninth flipped seat that gives the party a 56-44 majority. House Democrats formally nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, and incoming Oversight chair Robert Garcia sent document-preservation letters to Trump allies ahead of planned investigations. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, valuing the company at $1.5 trillion. Lawmakers pressed Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin about last week's ground stop, as the FAA suspended installing routers it believes overloaded communications. The NSA's classified network has been down since at least Tuesday in what the agency calls a temporary degradation. The White House dropped Heidi Overton's nomination to lead the FDA. A slow-moving storm flooded South Florida and collapsed a synagogue roof.

Abroad, Iran widened its Gulf attacks, targeting a U.S. air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain after American strikes on Qeshm Island. President Trump landed in Shenzhen, where Xi Jinping greeted him on the tarmac before a first three-way meeting with Xi and Vladimir Putin set for Thursday at the APEC summit. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is also attending amid tense relations with Beijing. Trump's Board of Peace told the UN Security Council that Israel and Hamas have failed to meet ceasefire commitments. Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed forces along their shared border. About 146,000 people joined cost-of-living protests across France, and Italy gave final approval to an antisemitism law.

fact.answer:
Leaves look green because they are packed with chlorophyll, the pigment that captures sunlight so the tree can make food. As days shorten and temperatures drop in autumn, the tree stops making chlorophyll and sends an enzyme that breaks down what is left, so the green fades.

The yellows and oranges are not new: those pigments were in the leaf all along, hidden by the green. Carotene, the pigment behind orange leaves, is the same one that makes carrots orange. Before the leaves drop, the tree also pulls their remaining nutrients back into its branches and trunk.

Weather shapes the show. A rainy season makes colors pop, and a cool fall makes red maples look brighter. But drought or an early frost can make leaves fall before they have time to change.
